questions.text: What makes a one-step temporal-difference update different from Monte Carlo evaluation?

options.A: TD waits for a full episode; MC updates after each transition.
options.B: TD uses a model of all transitions; MC uses only a reward function.
options.C: TD bootstraps from an estimated next-state value after one step.
options.D: TD never discounts future rewards; MC always discounts them.

questions.explanation: TD updates after a transition using r+γV(s′), while Monte Carlo waits for the complete sampled return.

questions.text: In a noisy tabular task, Q-learning repeatedly overestimates the best next action because it takes a maximum over noisy Q values. Which change addresses this specific bias?

options.A: Use Double Q-learning with separate value estimates for action selection and evaluation.
options.B: Increase ε until every action is chosen with equal probability forever.
options.C: Use γ=1 so future rewards receive no discount.
options.D: Replace the maximum with the minimum Q value in the same table.

questions.explanation: Double Q-learning reduces maximization bias by decoupling selection from evaluation using two value estimates.

questions.text: SARSA has Q(s,a)=2, reward r=1, γ=0.5, α=0.5, and Q(s_next,a_next)=4 for the action actually chosen next. What is the updated Q(s,a)?
questions.explanation: The SARSA target is 1 + 0.5×4 = 3; the update is 2 + 0.5×(3−2)=2.5.
